title: LEGO Technic blind boxes reportedly lack scan codes in Australia
summary: Fans in Australia say the new LEGO Technic Mighty Machines blind boxes don't have the usual scannable codes, meaning there's no way to peek at what's inside before buying. It's a rumour for now, sourced from a Reddit report.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to a Reddit user, boxes of 42233 Mighty Machines - LEGO Technic's first go at a Collectible Minifigures-style blind box format - are missing the usual scannable data matrix codes when sold in Australia. Instead, the base of the box reportedly only has the standard barcode found on all LEGO products.

Each Mighty Machines box contains one of eight tiny Technic models at random, and in most regions a scannable code lets curious buyers (or scalpers) check the contents before opening. If this report is accurate, Australian shoppers won't have that option and will have to buy blind, as LEGO presumably intended.

This isn't the first time fans in Australia have had a rougher deal with blind-box products - Collectible Minifigures series typically launch a month later there than elsewhere.

**This is currently a rumour**, based on a single Reddit report rather than any official LEGO statement, so treat it as unconfirmed until more buyers or retailers weigh in.

## Why it matters
Scannable codes have become a handy (if slightly against-the-spirit-of-blind-boxes) tool for collectors wanting specific figures or models without opening multiple boxes. If LEGO is quietly removing them in some markets, it could signal a wider rollback - bad news for collectors who rely on scanning to track down exact pieces, and a change worth watching if you build or collect Technic or Minifigures lines.

## What to watch next
The next real test will be 71053 Shrek Minifigures, due September 1 in most regions but likely arriving in Australia around October. If that series also ships without scannable codes there, it'll add weight to this being a deliberate shift rather than a one-off packaging issue with Mighty Machines.

title: Rumour: LEGO Ideas Wallace & Gromit set may stay close to its original size
summary: Leaked details suggest the upcoming LEGO Ideas Wallace & Gromit model will have around 1,038 pieces and cost $99.99, launching 1 October — with far fewer changes from fan design to final set than recent Ideas models.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Rumour: according to Brick Fanatics, the highly anticipated LEGO Ideas Wallace & Gromit set — based on a fan design by Pidelium — is said to include around 1,038 pieces, cost $99.99, and launch on 1 October. None of this has been officially confirmed by LEGO yet.

The original fan submission was capped at a maximum of 1,000 elements as part of its Ideas challenge, and the exact piece count was never revealed, only that it stayed under that limit. If the rumoured 1,038-piece figure is accurate, that means the finished set may have grown by just 38 pieces or so from the original pitch — a notably small change compared with other recent LEGO Ideas buildable figures.

For comparison, 21372 La Catrina reportedly shrank to roughly half its original size, 21370 E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial dropped from a huge 2,990-element fan design down to 1,226 pieces in the final set, and 21361 Gremlins: Gizmo actually grew from 400 elements to 1,125 pieces. Wallace & Gromit, by contrast, looks set to stay much truer to its original scale — though small tweaks within the rumoured piece count are still possible.

Importantly, LEGO has not officially announced the Wallace & Gromit Ideas set at all yet, so all of the above remains unconfirmed.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas fans often see big differences between a winning fan design and the final retail set, in both size and price. If this rumour holds up, it suggests LEGO is aiming to preserve the spirit and scale of Pidelium's original Wallace & Gromit concept — good news for fans who backed the project hoping for a faithful adaptation, and a useful data point for anyone trying to predict pricing and piece counts on future Ideas sets.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for LEGO's official announcement of the Wallace & Gromit Ideas set, which should confirm (or correct) the piece count, price and release date mentioned here.

title: LEGO Ideas review round grows again with Taylor Swift and fruit basket projects
summary: Four more fan designs, including another Taylor Swift concept and a fruit-themed build, have joined LEGO Ideas' second 2026 review round after passing 10,000 supporters.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Ideas' second 2026 review round has picked up four fresh entries after each design crossed the 10,000-supporter threshold needed to be considered for an official set.

The new additions are:
- **Taylor Swift's Disk Collection: Eras Tour Edition** by FearsomeBuilder020 – another attempt at bringing the singer into the LEGO portfolio, this time using decorated elements to represent Eras Tour album covers
- **Manifest "Amatör/Amateur"** by MMBDCD
- **The Bridge Village** by CoasterZoom
- **Fruits Basket** by Jagamax, the designer behind the previously released 40788 Friendly Snails set

This brings the current review round to well over a dozen projects in total, spanning everything from pop culture (Jumanji, Twister, Wacky Races) to nature-themed builds and video game tributes like Deltarune and Terraria.

It's worth noting reaching 10,000 supporters only means a project enters LEGO's review stage - it does not guarantee the set will be produced. Multiple Taylor Swift concepts have hit this milestone before without success.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is one of the few routes for fan-designed concepts to become genuine, mass-produced LEGO sets, so a busy review round is good news for anyone hoping to see their favourite niche idea turned into bricks. For collectors, it's also a reminder to keep an eye on which projects survive the review process, as successful ones often become sought-after sets down the line.

## What to watch next
LEGO typically announces the results of an Ideas review round some months after voting closes, so it could be a while before we learn whether any of these projects - Taylor Swift included - make the cut. Bricks in a Bag will keep tracking updates as the review round develops.

title: Fan builder recreates Duel of the Fates in 15,000 LEGO bricks
summary: Custom builder Kyle Collard has followed up last year's award-winning prequel diorama with a fresh Star Wars MOC, this time capturing the Duel of the Fates from The Phantom Menace.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan builder Kyle Collard (known online as LordofVador) has completed a new LEGO Star Wars diorama depicting the Duel of the Fates from The Phantom Menace — the moment Qui-Gon Jinn falls and Obi-Wan looks on helplessly. The build uses around 15,000 LEGO bricks and took roughly six months to complete, combining detailed building techniques with LED lighting for extra atmosphere.

This is a follow-up to Collard's previous diorama depicting the climax of the prequel trilogy, which made The Brothers Brick's best-of-2025 shortlist. The new build has also won him Best Star Wars Scene at Texas' Brick Rodeo event for a second time, meaning he's retained the title.

This is a fan-made custom creation (MOC), not an official LEGO Group product.

## Why it matters
This showcases what's possible with large-scale custom brick dioramas and advanced lighting techniques — great inspiration for anyone into display builds, Star Wars scenes, or ambitious personal projects. It's also a nice reminder that fan competitions like Brick Rodeo continue to spotlight standout custom work in the community.

## What to watch next
Worth keeping an eye out for whether Collard shares build details, techniques, or instructions, and whether he continues this apparent series of Star Wars duel dioramas.

title: Fan-built Kraken Knights tower brings LEGO Castle faction to life
summary: Builder Gabriel Midgely (Noldor Lego) has created a striking hexagonal tower MOC for the Kraken Knights faction, built for the Summer Joust competition's 'No Bley' category.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Custom LEGO builder Gabriel Midgely, known online as Noldor Lego, has unveiled an impressive fan-made tower for the Kraken Knights, one of the newer Castle factions LEGO introduced last year alongside the Horse, Snake and Griffon crests.

The build is a hexagonal tower using cheese slopes and SNOT (studs-not-on-top) techniques to create clean, sloping corners. A colour gradient above and below an implied waterline gives the tower a real sense of place, while tall, spindly pylons create a distinctive silhouette. Hidden merfolk swimming around the base add an extra layer of storytelling, hinting at a possible relationship with the Knights above.

The MOC was built for the "No Bley" category of the Summer Joust building competition, where builders avoid the trans-Neptunium blue/grey/black 'bley' colour palette. Nougat and dark orange tones were chosen to complement the Kraken Knights' green minifigure uniforms.

Midgely, who works as a concept artist, has also produced an illustration bringing the Kraken Knights minifigure to life beyond the brick model. This is a fan creation and is not an official LEGO Group release.

## Why it matters
Official LEGO Castle sets for newer factions like the Kraken Knights have been limited, so fan builders are stepping in to flesh out the lore and aesthetics themselves. It's a good example of how the custom-building community keeps niche themes alive with fresh building techniques, colour choices and worldbuilding that official sets haven't yet explored.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on Summer Joust competition results and more MOCs from Noldor Lego, who has built a reputation for strong Castle-themed creations.

title: LEGO Technic Mighty Machines: why the blind-box is bigger than usual
summary: LEGO Technic's new 42233 Mighty Machines Series 1 blind boxes are noticeably larger than standard minifigure boxes, and there's a good reason for it.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Technic's new 42233 Mighty Machines Series 1 collectable vehicles have launched, priced at £4.49 per blind-boxed model. A side-by-side comparison shared by a Reddit user shows the box is considerably bigger than the one used for 71052 Series 29 minifigures.

The larger size makes sense once you consider what's inside: these are buildable Technic vehicles with bigger elements than a standard minifigure, plus a game card that needs to sit flat in the box. It's worth noting this isn't the first time LEGO has used an oversized blind-box format — the previous run of buildable Super Mario figures reportedly used what looks like an identical box design. Interestingly, the buildable 71049 F1 Collectible Race Cars managed to fit into the smaller, standard-sized boxes.

The boxes also carry a scannable code on the base, a feature that had already been revealed ahead of launch and works with the Brick Search app for both Minifigures and Mighty Machines lines.

## Why it matters
If you're planning a trip to your local LEGO Store to pick up a few blind boxes, knowing they're bigger than usual is genuinely useful — they'll take up more space in your bag or backpack than a typical minifigure box would. It also helps explain the higher price point compared to standard Collectible Minifigures.

## What to watch next
LEGO's next blind-box collectable, 71053 Shrek, launches on 1 September — it'll be worth seeing whether that line sticks with the standard smaller box or follows the bigger Mighty Machines format.
